reviews.review: A fantastic hack 'n slash game for any Warhammer enthustiastic

Even the heretic can be redimed in DEATH.
for the immortal good emperor of mankind.

p.s. fun game 7/10
It is a very good game with a lot of fun, i recommend it for all warhammer 40k fans and all those who want a good action game.

I hate it when a game has a combined DLC price higher than the game itself (Koei Tecmos, I’m looking at you!). It makes the game feel like bait.
But in this case the DLC is for Multiplayer, so for socially awkward people like me, the single player is good enough. And in that respect, it’s a good campaign. Damn good. Filled with Epic Moments and Zealous Devotion to the Emperor.
 Still, I don’t like Gameworkshop and their rabid copy wright over English words, but I gotta recognize when a game is good.
This one expects and requires you to rush, cut, bash and finish the enemies of the Emperor in displays of strength and might. Disgrace and penalties await you if you go the cowards way of hiding behind a box shooting.
I got this game on a magazine for 5€, but it’s worth more.
Kill those Xenos not because you have too, but because it fills your murder bonner to burst!

I re-completed this game on Hard some time ago, and though it was somewhat fun while it lasted, the game is, in fact, far from perfect in most aspects.

The most obvious flaw of the game is its repetitivity. Throughout the story different weapons and enchancements become available, sure, but essentially the gameplay situations themselves are becoming more and more of a deja vu as you proceed.

[list]
  [*] You jump into some new portion of terrain. There are Ork. You have to battle through their forces to reach a more powerful group of Ork, then you either interact with something or get a vox-transmission from your allies, and the next portion of terrain (and Ork) unlocks.

  [*] You reach a relatively vast area with a passage which is locked. You have to reflect an enemy attack to proceed (sometimes one of your followers are busy with certain story action while you cover them). There is always an elevated area you cannot get to, from which the waves of enemies come.

  [*] You are trapped in an arena-shaped location. A boss calls in waves of enemies. When you are done with them, he gets to you and you have to complete a QTE for a cinematographic KO.
[/list]

There are some refreshing moments, like jetpack riding, but they are like dessert, before which you always get to eat another full pot of porridge. Perhaps, it would be less noticeable if the game would turn out to be less absurd by both the terms of WH40K canon and mere common sense.

[list]
  [*] A forge-world, the marvel of imperial engineering, basically supposed to be a giant temple of Omnissiah, is protected by imperial guardsmen instead of Legiones Skitarii. I mean, how lore ignorant could that possibly be? It`s essentially like guarding a Pentagon with one 80-year old grandpa with a pre-WWII hunting rifle.

  [*] _Three_ space marines dealing first with an entire Ork WAAAAGH, warboss included, then [spoiler] with a warband of a prized Chaos champion followers, the champion himself included, too[/spoiler], is this an actual game storyline or a teenage fanfiction? If things worked that way, none would dare attack any imperial world - there are certainly enough space marines to put just three of them to guard each planet.

  [*] [spoiler]An Ultramarine captain tells his fellow Ultramarine he did wrong by strictly abiding the Codex.[/spoiler] I wonder if the developers just happened to run into a list of bad WH40K-themed jokes and thought they would paste them into the script - or rather just make them a script.
[/list]

Overall, the singleplayer part of the game is just not worth the pain. The multiplayer has a lot less sharp edges and generally allows more diversity, but still looks like a semi-serious wannabe-Warhammer game, with power armor painted all colours of rainbow (acceptable for Chaos, but nonsense for loyalists) and a pretty standard, though entertaining, gameplay. There is also Dreadnought assault, but finding an active game is extreme luck. Whoever finds himself a fan of the 40K universe should probably only buy this with a major discount.
